introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0510 Biology 1, June 2020, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Duration: one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section I (questions 1-7): independent questions. Section II (questions 8-20): biological diagrams. Section III (questions 21-25): one or more responses correct. Section IV (questions 26-30): pairs of statements. Section V (questions 31-40): lettered headings and a description. Section VI (questions 41-50): biological situations.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION I - directions as printed, summarised:* Each of these questions or incomplete statements is followed by four suggested answers. Select the best answer in each case.

Movement of water molecules from a region of high concentration of water molecules to a region of low concentration of water molecules is
questions.corrige_markdown: This describes osmosis: net movement of water molecules from a region of high water concentration to one of low water concentration, usually across a partially permeable membrane. Diffusion (B) is the general movement of any particles; absorption (A) is uptake of substances; osmoregulation (D) is the control of the water balance of the body. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What occurs when the leaves of a plant lose more water than the plant gets from the soil?
questions.corrige_markdown: When transpiration exceeds water uptake, the cells lose turgor and the leaves and stems droop: this is wilting. Plasmolysis (B) is the shrinking of the cell contents away from the wall in a strong solution; turgidity (C) is the opposite state (cells full of water); guttation (D) is loss of liquid water from leaf margins. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following processes uses up energy?
questions.corrige_markdown: Active transport moves substances against a concentration gradient and needs energy (ATP) from respiration. Enzymatic digestion, osmosis and ultra-filtration (which is driven by blood pressure) do not use cell energy directly. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The parts of the mammalian heart containing oxygenated blood are the
questions.corrige_markdown: Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium and passes to the left ventricle. The right atrium and right ventricle carry deoxygenated blood. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Chloroplast of plant cells
questions.corrige_markdown: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy used in photosynthesis. Food storage is mainly by leucoplasts and vacuoles, and the cell wall (not the chloroplast) maintains the shape of the cell. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
One method of spread of AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) is

*Options as printed:* A) Through Screened blood transfusion   B) Exchange of sterilized surgical equipment (blades, needles)   C) During pregnancy.   D) During unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person.
questions.corrige_markdown:
HIV is spread by unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person. Screened blood and sterilised equipment are safe (A and B are prevention measures). Option C is incomplete: HIV can pass from an infected mother to the child during pregnancy, birth or breast feeding, but the statement as printed does not say the mother is infected, so D is the best answer.

**Intended answer: D (During unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Causes Malaria
questions.corrige_markdown: Malaria is caused by the protozoan parasite Plasmodium. The female Anopheles mosquito (A) is only the vector that carries it. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION II - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions relates to biological diagrams. Select the best answer for each question.

In the diagram of an amoeba, the contractile vacuole functions in
questions.corrige_markdown: The contractile vacuole of a freshwater amoeba collects excess water that enters by osmosis and expels it, so it regulates the water content of the cell: osmoregulation. (The diagram mentioned in the question is not reproduced in the scanned paper, but the answer depends only on the function of the contractile vacuole.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
This concerns the nitrogen cycle shown below:

![fig-1](gce-ol-biology-2020-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

What process is represented by arrow 3?
questions.corrige_markdown: Arrow 3 runs from the box "Nitrates in the soil" to the box "Nitrogen in the atmosphere": nitrates are converted back into nitrogen gas by denitrifying bacteria. This is denitrification. Nitrogen fixation (B) would go from atmospheric nitrogen to nitrates (the long curved arrow), and nitrification (C) turns ammonium into nitrates. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is a food chain in a garden ecosystem.

Cabbage → Caterpillar → Hen → Hawk

Identify the herbivore in the food chain
questions.corrige_markdown: A herbivore eats plants only. The caterpillar eats cabbage (a producer); the hen and the hawk are carnivores/secondary and tertiary consumers. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Spirogyra is autotrophic because of the presence of
questions.corrige_markdown: Spirogyra makes its own food by photosynthesis because its cells contain a spiral chloroplast with chlorophyll. The pyrenoids are only starch-storage bodies in the chloroplast. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: This structure in the eye has a high concentration of light sensitive cells (rods and cones)
questions.corrige_markdown: The retina is the inner layer of the eye that carries the rods (dim light) and cones (colour, bright light). The choroid contains blood vessels and pigment, the sclera is the tough protective white layer and the cornea is the transparent front. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Transports oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart in the mammalian circulatory system.
questions.corrige_markdown: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. The pulmonary artery takes deoxygenated blood to the lungs (a common trap), the aorta takes oxygenated blood from the heart to the body, and the vena cava brings deoxygenated blood from the body. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An endocrine gland in the human body that produces a hormone which increases the rate of heart beat
questions.corrige_markdown: The adrenal glands secrete adrenaline, which increases the heart rate (fight or flight response). The thyroid controls metabolic rate, the pancreas controls blood sugar and the pituitary controls other glands. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Produces an oily secretion in the skin which keeps it supple.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sebaceous gland secretes sebum, an oily substance that keeps the skin and hair supple and waterproof. The sweat gland makes sweat, Meissner's corpuscle is a touch receptor and the subcutaneous layer stores fat. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which part of the mammalian brain is responsible for voluntary (conscious) activities of the body?
questions.corrige_markdown: The cerebrum controls voluntary actions, thinking, memory and conscious sensation. The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions (breathing, heartbeat) and the hypothalamus controls temperature and water balance. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which structure in the brain is responsible for balance and posture?
questions.corrige_markdown: The cerebellum coordinates muscular movement, balance and posture. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is the diagram of part of the human digestive system.

![fig-2](gce-ol-biology-2020-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

How is structure 3 important in homeostasis?
questions.corrige_markdown: Structure 1 is the liver, 2 the stomach and 3 the pancreas, lying under the stomach beside the duodenum. In homeostasis the pancreas (islets of Langerhans) secretes insulin, which lowers blood glucose. Deamination, detoxification and breakdown of red blood cells are functions of the liver (structure 1). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which structure in the male reproductive system produces sperms?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sperms are made in the seminiferous tubules of the testes. The epididymis only stores and matures them, the prostate gland adds fluid and the penis delivers semen. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why does the left ventricle of the mammalian heart have thicker walls?
questions.corrige_markdown: The left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body (a long distance, high pressure), so it needs a thick muscular wall; the right ventricle only sends blood to the nearby lungs. Both ventricles hold the same volume (A is wrong) and the blood is under high, not low, pressure (D). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It pumps blood over a long distance.
It carries blood loaded with food and Oxygen.
It carries blood under low pressure.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION III - directions as printed, summarised:* For each question, ONE or MORE of the responses is (are) correct. Decide which responses are correct, then choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are all correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

Unicellular organisms lack a transport system because

1. They have a large surface area to volume ratio.
2. Substances diffuse over short distances in them.
3. Their body makes intimate contact with their surroundings.
questions.corrige_markdown: All three statements are correct: a unicellular organism has a large surface area to volume ratio, so substances pass in and out quickly; the distances are so short that diffusion is enough; and the single cell is in direct contact with its surroundings. **Answer: A (1, 2 and 3 are all correct).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Mature Red Blood Cells

1. Function in transport
2. Lack nucleus
3. Lack haemoglobin
questions.corrige_markdown: Mature mammalian red blood cells transport oxygen (1 correct) and have lost their nucleus to make room for haemoglobin (2 correct). Statement 3 is false: they are full of haemoglobin, which carries the oxygen. **Answer: B (1 and 2 only).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
During inspiration,

1. The diaphragm muscle contracts.
2. The pressure in the lungs decreases.
3. The rib cage moves upwards and outwards.
questions.corrige_markdown: During inspiration the diaphragm contracts and flattens, the external intercostal muscles raise the rib cage upwards and outwards, the chest volume increases and so the pressure in the lungs falls below atmospheric pressure, drawing air in. All three are correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
During overheating,

1. Superficial blood vessels constrict.
2. More sweat is produced.
3. Erector pili muscle relaxes.
questions.corrige_markdown: When the body overheats, superficial (skin) blood vessels dilate (vasodilation), not constrict, so statement 1 is false. More sweat is produced (2 correct) and the erector pili muscles relax so the hairs lie flat (3 correct). **Answer: C (2 and 3 only).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
To focus on near objects

1. The ciliary muscle contracts.
2. The suspensory ligament slackens.
3. The lens becomes thicker.
questions.corrige_markdown: For near vision the ciliary muscle contracts, which slackens the suspensory ligaments, so the elastic lens becomes thicker (more convex) and bends the light more strongly. All three are correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Choose: A if both are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first; B if both are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C if the first is true and the second false; D if the first is false and the second true.

**First statement:** Gametes are generally produced by mitosis.

**Second statement:** Body cells are produced by mitosis.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: gametes are produced by meiosis (reduction division), which halves the chromosome number. The second statement is true: body (somatic) cells are made by mitosis for growth and repair. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** The image of an object formed on the retina is inverted.

**Second statement:** Light sensitive cells are found on the retina.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true: the lens forms a real, inverted image on the retina, and the rods and cones are on the retina. But the presence of light-sensitive cells does not explain why the image is inverted (that is due to the refraction of light by the cornea and lens). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** In Phototropism, the stimulus is gravity

**Second statement:** Shoots are positively phototropic
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: in phototropism the stimulus is light (gravity is the stimulus in geotropism). The second statement is true: shoots grow towards light. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Short sightedness occurs when an individual can only see objects clearly when they are close to the eye.

**Second statement:** Short sightedness is corrected using concave or diverging lens
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true: a short-sighted person sees near objects clearly but distant ones blurred, and the defect is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens. However, the correction is not the explanation of the defect (the cause is an eyeball that is too long or a lens that is too strong, so the image forms in front of the retina). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** The bicuspid and tricuspid valves close when the ventricles contract.

**Second statement:** Valves close to prevent backflow of blood.

*Options as printed:* A) True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.   B) True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.   C) True, False.   D) False, True.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. During ventricular contraction the pressure in the ventricles rises above that in the atria, forcing the atrioventricular valves shut, and the purpose of this closure is to stop blood flowing back into the atria. The second statement is therefore most probably intended as the explanation (key A), but a strict reader could say that it does not explain why the valves close when the ventricles contract (key B), so the question is left open for self-assessment. Most likely intended key: **A**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION V - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of four lettered headings A, B, C, D. Select the heading which is closely related to the description which follows.

The immediate end-products of photosynthesis.
questions.corrige_markdown: Photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water, in light and chlorophyll, gives glucose + oxygen. Glucose and oxygen are therefore the immediate products; starch is made later from glucose, and carbon dioxide and water are the raw materials. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Involves extracellular digestion.
questions.corrige_markdown: Saprophytes (for example Mucor, mushrooms) secrete digestive enzymes onto dead organic matter and absorb the digested products: digestion takes place outside the cells (extracellular). Holozoic nutrition involves ingestion and internal digestion, and holophytic nutrition is photosynthesis. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Elimination of harmful organisms using other living organisms.
questions.corrige_markdown: Biological control uses a living organism (a predator, parasite or pathogen) to eliminate a pest. Chemical control uses chemicals such as pesticides. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Its large proportion in the atmosphere causes greenhouse effect.
questions.corrige_markdown: Carbon dioxide, released in large amounts by burning fossil fuels and by deforestation, traps heat in the atmosphere and is the main cause of the greenhouse effect. Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide cause acid rain, and carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: All the living organisms in a locality.
questions.corrige_markdown: A community is all the populations of living organisms (plants and animals) in a habitat. An ecosystem also includes the non-living environment; a population is a single species in the area. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Adds carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
questions.corrige_markdown: Decay (decomposition by bacteria and fungi, which respire) releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the air, and digestion and deamination do not release it into the atmosphere. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The washing down of nutrients from top soil to sub soil.
questions.corrige_markdown: Leaching is the washing down of soluble mineral nutrients (nitrates, for example) by rain water from the top soil into the sub soil. Erosion removes the soil itself. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The reason why spirogyra is autotrophic.
questions.corrige_markdown: Spirogyra is autotrophic because it contains chlorophyll (in its chloroplast), which lets it make food by photosynthesis. Pyrenoids and starch are only storage structures or products. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Represents the correct flow of energy in a locality.
questions.corrige_markdown: Energy flows from the producer (lettuce) to the primary consumer (grasshopper, which eats lettuce), then to a secondary consumer (chicken eats the grasshopper) and a tertiary consumer (hawk eats the chicken). Only option C follows these feeding links in order. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Will produce a brick red precipitate when tested with Benedict's solution.
questions.corrige_markdown: Benedict's solution, heated, turns brick red with a reducing sugar such as glucose. Starch solution gives no colour change (it needs iodine), and egg white (protein) is tested with biuret reagent. Bean extract is mostly starch and protein, so it does not give the clear brick-red precipitate. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION VI - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions deals with biological situations. Each situation is followed by a set of questions. Select the best answer for each question.

The set up below was used as a control experiment to show that carbon dioxide is necessary for photosynthesis.

![fig-3](gce-ol-biology-2020-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

The caustic soda in the setup is to
questions.corrige_markdown: Caustic soda (sodium hydroxide) absorbs carbon dioxide. It is placed in the air inlet and in the dish beside the plant so that the plant receives no carbon dioxide, and the result shows whether photosynthesis (starch formation) needs carbon dioxide. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Fish suffocate out of water. This is due to
questions.corrige_markdown: Out of water the gill filaments collapse and stick together, so the surface area is greatly reduced and the gills cannot absorb oxygen from the air. Air contains far more oxygen than water, so B is false. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Less oxygen on land than in water.
Gills not absorbing oxygen from air.

questions.enonce_markdown: In testing a leaf for the presence of starch, the leaf is boiled in alcohol for 5 minutes to
questions.corrige_markdown: Hot alcohol dissolves the green chlorophyll so that the colour change with iodine solution can be seen clearly (blue-black if starch is present). The leaf is softened earlier by dipping it in boiling water. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In setting up a potometer, it is important to cut and mount the leafy shoot under water so as to
questions.corrige_markdown: Cutting under water stops air from being drawn into the xylem vessels, which would form an air lock and break the continuous water column, so the potometer would not measure water uptake properly. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Prevent the entry of air bubbles into the xylem.
Prevent water flowing backwards in the shoot.
Ensure sufficient supply of water to the shoot.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the probability that a couple with genotypes BO and AB will have a child of blood group B?
questions.corrige_markdown: Gametes: B or O from the first parent, A or B from the second. Offspring: BA (group AB), BB (group B), OA (group A), OB (group B). Two of the four equally likely genotypes (BB and OB) give group B: probability 2/4 = 1/2. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-4](gce-ol-biology-2020-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

The bean seedling placed on a rotating clinostat in the diagram grows straight upwards because of
questions.corrige_markdown: A clinostat rotates the seedling slowly, so every side is exposed to light (and to gravity) for equal times. Auxin is then distributed evenly, all sides elongate equally and the shoot grows straight upwards. Unequal auxin (A or C) would make the shoot bend. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: High concentration of auxin on the illuminated side.
High concentration of auxin on darker side.

questions.enonce_markdown: The terminal bud of a tomato plant was cut off. Which of the following would have been observed?
questions.corrige_markdown: The terminal bud makes auxin that suppresses the axillary (lateral) buds (apical dominance). When it is cut off, the inhibition is removed and the axillary buds grow fast, so the plant becomes bushy. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Plants always occur at the first trophic level in food chains. This is because
questions.corrige_markdown: Plants are producers: by photosynthesis they convert solar energy into chemical energy in food, which is the starting point of every food chain. The other options are not the reason (and plants are autotrophic, not saprophytic). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Plants were the first organisms on earth.
Plants are found all over the world.
Plants convert solar energy into chemical energy

questions.enonce_markdown: Lime water turns milky when exhaled air is bubbled through it. This indicates that exhaled air
questions.corrige_markdown: Lime water (calcium hydroxide solution) turns milky because carbon dioxide forms insoluble calcium carbonate. This shows that exhaled air contains carbon dioxide. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Exposed palm wine loses its sweetness after several hours. This is due to
questions.corrige_markdown: Wild yeast in the palm sap carries out anaerobic respiration (alcoholic fermentation): sugar becomes ethanol and carbon dioxide, so the wine loses its sweetness. Sugar is not converted to starch (B) and evaporation (C) does not remove sugar. Bacteria (D) also act on palm wine, but they turn it sour (acids), whereas the loss of sweetness is the work of yeast. **Answer: A.**
